_what: fusion's compliance-guard configuration for THIS project. The guard hooks read it from the project root, on every guarded tool call, and merge it over the plugin's own hooks/config.json and then over fusion's built-in defaults. Keys the parser does not recognise are carried through untouched and never reported, which is why these underscore-prefixed notes can live in the file itself. The one exception is a key fusion has RETIRED — a key that used to configure something and no longer does. A retired key is reported on every guarded call until you delete the line, because a key that is inert AND silent would leave you believing a setting is in force when the mechanism behind it is gone. See _override for the one that exists today.
_override: To change something, add the key you want to change, in the same shape the plugin's hooks/config.json uses for it. The merge is per LEAF, not per object: a key you declare is taken exactly as you wrote it, and a key you leave out — even inside an object you did declare — inherits the plugin's value first and falls back to fusion's built-in default only when neither file speaks. So {"guard":{"defaultSensitivity":"high"}} raises the sensitivity and keeps every other guard setting the plugin ships. Narrowing works because a declared value wins outright: {"guard":{"categoryPaths":{}}} really is the empty object, on purpose, not an inheritance. A value with the wrong type is dropped and named in a guard advisory, then inherits as if you had omitted it; a file that is not valid JSON is dropped and reported the same way, never ignored in silence. ONE KEY IS RETIRED: guard.protectedPaths. fusion removed the protected-path mechanism it configured, so the guard no longer watches a list of paths and nothing is protected by naming it here. If your file still carries that key you get one advisory naming it on every guarded call until you delete the line; everything else in your file goes on working while it is there.
_turnBudget: Not everything this file configures is the guard. "orchestrator": {"maxTurns": N} is the number of Turns the orchestrator's Phase-2 loop may run before its Max-Turns circuit breaker exits the loop and reports what is left. It merges by the same per-leaf rule as everything above, and it is read once per session by bin/fusion-turn-budget at the orchestrator's Setup — no hook reads it. fusion's own budget is defined in exactly one place, the DEFAULTS in the plugin's hooks/lib/config.ts, and is deliberately not restated in the plugin's hooks/config.json or in any agent prompt, so this file is the only place a project changes it. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more — 0, a negative, a decimal, a string — is dropped and named in an advisory, then inherits as if it were absent; there is no upper bound, because a project that wants 60 Turns has said so in a git-tracked file.
_guardEnabled: guard.enabled is the one key this file may not set. The guard's on/off switch is read from the plugin layer and fusion's defaults only — a project does not switch off the guard that governs it. A declared value, true or false, is ignored, and the loader reports the ignored key in a guard advisory naming it, on every guarded call until the line is removed, so the key is never silently inert.
_gitTracked: This file belongs in version control, and that is the point of it living at the project root. It decides how sensitively the guard reads the decisions you record here, when it escalates to a halt, and how many Turns the orchestrator may run — so every change to it has to appear in a diff and pass through the same review as the rest of the project. The diff is now the ONLY thing that bounds it. fusion used to defend this file against its own agents: the guard added it to the protected list as soon as it existed and wrote back any change an agent made to it. That defence went with the protected-path mechanism, so an agent can edit this file like any other, and the git history is where you see that one did.
